subsections.label: E
subsections.title: This section (2020.2) shall not authorize the
paragraphs: establishment of commercial gravel pits or quarries. Furthermore, within the 100 year flood plains of the LaPlatte River, McCabe's Brook and Monroe Brook, excavations of earth materials shall be prohibited where the activity proposed will lower the level of the water table, interfere with the natural flow patterns or reduce the flood stage capacity.

subsections.label: F
subsections.title: Sections 2020.2 A- 2020.2E notwithstanding, the
paragraphs: provisions of this Section shall not apply to the removal of natural resources from a farm operation, nursery, or cemetery to the extent that such removal is necessary to the operation of the same.

sections.title: Certificates of Occupancy:
New Buildings - No building hereafter erected shall be occupied or
paragraphs: used, in whole or in part, for any purpose whatever, until a certificate of occupancy shall have been issued by the administrative officer, certifying that such building conforms to Page XX- 9 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW Article XX Effective May 18, 2016 any approved permits, plans, and specifications and the requirements of these regulations.

sections.title: Alterations of Buildings - No building hereafter altered, which was
paragraphs: vacant during the progress of the work of alteration, shall be occupied or used, in whole or in part, for any purpose whatever, until a certificate of occupancy shall have been issued by the administrative officer certifying that the work for which the permit was issued was completed in accordance with the approved plans and specifications and the requirements of these regulations.

sections.title: Residential Accessory Structures
paragraphs: . Certificates of Occupancy shall not be required for residential accessory structures.

sections.title: As-Built Drawings
paragraphs: . "As- built" drawings or plans shall be provided as part of all applications seeking Certificates of Occupancy for commercial or industrial structures having gross building footprints of 5,000 or more square feet .

sections.title: Expiration of Permits and Approvals:
Zoning Permits - The following provisions shall apply to zoning
paragraphs: permits:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: A zoning permit shall expire two years from its date of
paragraphs: issuance unless there is a reasonable amount of objective evidence of intent to complete the project for which the permit was issued. It shall be deemed presumptive evidence of an intent to complete the project if at least fifty (50) percent of the total estimated project costs have been expended in construction and site improvements.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: A zoning permit may be extended by the administrative officer
paragraphs: for a period of one year, upon a finding of an intent to complete. A zoning permit may not be extended more than one year beyond the two years specified in paragraph 2040.1.A above.

sections.title: Variances, Conditional Use and Site Plan Approvals
paragraphs: - Variances, Conditional Use and Site Plan Approvals will expire two years from their date of issuance. The actions authorized by the Variance or Site plan may be extended for one year only by the administrative officer if it is demonstrated that the delays were beyond the control of the applicant, and that conditions affecting and addressed by the approvals have not changed. Page XX- 10 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW Article XX Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Planned Unit Developments - The following provisions shall
paragraphs: apply to Planned Unit Developments:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Approvals for Planned Unit Developments shall normally
paragraphs: expire two years from their date of approval. However, the Development Review Board may extend the life of such approvals when it is clear at the outset that the project will be phased or will require a construction period greater than two years. The term of the approval shall not be set longer than the proposed phasing plan or estimated construction period.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Approvals for Planned Unit Developments may be extended
paragraphs: for up to two years beyond the original date of expiration set pursuant to 2040.3 A if the Development Review Board determines that substantial progress (fifty percent) has been made in completing the development, that the applicant intends to complete the development, and that the delays were beyond the control of the applicant.

sections.title: Appeals
As per Section 4465 of the Vermont Planning and Development
paragraphs: Act, an interested person may appeal a decision of the administrative officer to the Development Review Board. Such appeal shall be filed, processed and heard in conformance with the provisions of the Vermont Planning and Development Act.

sections.title: As per Sections 4471 of the Vermont Planning and Development
paragraphs: Act, decisions made by the Development Review Board may be appealed to the Vermont Environmental Court.

sections.title: Application and Fees
All applications under these regulations shall be made on forms
paragraphs: prescribed by the administrative officer, and shall be accompanied by the fees prescribed by resolution of the Town Board of Selectmen.

sections.title: Pursuant to 24 VSA S4440 (d), an applicant may be required to
paragraphs: pay the reasonable costs and fees incident to an independent technical review of the application. These costs and fees shall be paid by the applicant in a timely manner, upon presentation of a bill for services by the Town. Upon failure of an applicant to pay a Page XX- 11 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW Article XX Effective May 18, 2016 bill for technical review services in a timely manner, the Town shall record a copy of the same in the land records and said bill shall constitute a lien on the applicant's property that may be enforced in the same manner as a tax lien under 32 VSA subsection 5061.

sections.title: Before the Town engages the services of a person or firm to
paragraphs: conduct a specific independent technical review, it shall provide an applicant with notice of the same and an opportunity to be heard on any proposed review.

sections.title: Notice of Public Hearings
Public notice for conditional use review, variances, administrative
paragraphs: officer appeals, site plan reviews, and Planned Unit Development reviews shall be given not less than fifteen (15) days prior to the date of the public hearing by:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Publication, by the municipality, of the date, place,
paragraphs: and purpose of the hearing in a newspaper of general circulation in the municipality affected.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Posting of the same information in three or more
paragraphs: public places within the municipality in conformance with location requirements of 1 V.S.A. S 312(c)(2), including posting, by the applicant, within view from the public right-of-way most nearly adjacent to the property for which an application is made.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: The mailing of the same information by first class
paragraphs: mail to the applicant, any appellant, and owners of record of property contiguous to, or directly across any public right of way from, property that is the subject of the hearing. Stamped and addressed envelopes for each owner of record shall be provided to the Town by the applicant, which shall mail notices using the envelopes provided. Notices shall be accompanied by information that clearly informs the recipient where additional information may be obtained and indicating that participation in the local proceeding is a prerequisite to the right to take any subsequent appeal. Failure of a party to receive notice under this subsection shall not invalidate any action taken as a result of the public Page XX- 12 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW Article XX Effective May 18, 2016 hearing unless such notice is materially misleading or the failure/defect was the result of a deliberate or intentional act.

sections.title: Public notice for hearings on all other types of development review
paragraphs: shall be given not less than seven days prior to the date of the public hearing, and shall include at a minimum all the following:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Posting of the date, place, and purpose of the
paragraphs: hearing in three or more public places within the municipality in conformance with the time and location requirements of 1 V.S.A. S 312(c)(2).

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Written notification to the applicant and to the
paragraphs: owners of all properties adjoining the property subject to development, without regard to right-of- way. The notification shall include a description of the proposed project and shall be accompanied by information that clearly informs the recipient where additional information may be obtained, and that participation in the local proceeding is a prerequisite to the right to take any subsequent appeal.

sections.title: The applicant shall bear the cost of the public warning and the cost
paragraphs: and responsibility of notification of adjoining landowners. The applicant shall demonstrate proof of delivery to adjoining landowners either by certified mail, return receipt requested, or by written notice hand delivered or mailed to the last known address supported by a sworn certificate of service.

sections.title: No defect in the form or substance of any requirements in
paragraphs: subdivision (1) or (2) of this subsection shall invalidate the action of the appropriate municipal panel where reasonable efforts are made to provide adequate posting and notice. However, the action shall be invalid when the defective posting or notice was materially misleading in content. If an action is ruled to be invalid by the environmental court or by the applicable municipal panel itself, the action shall be remanded to the applicable municipal panel to provide new posting and notice, hold a new hearing, and take a new action.

sections.title: Implementation. These regulations shall become effective twenty one
paragraphs: (21) days after the date of adoption by the Selectboard. On the date these regulations become effective, they will amend in its entirety the Page XX- 13 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW Article XX Effective May 18, 2016 comprehensive revision of the Town of Shelburne Zoning Regulations adopted December 23, 1985 and last amended June 18, 2014. Page XX- 14 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: General. Definitions contained in the Vermont Planning and Development Act shall
paragraphs: be applicable throughout these regulations unless otherwise specifically defined in this Section.

sections.title: Specific Definitions
Accessory Apartment - A dwelling unit located within or appurtenant to and clearly
paragraphs: subordinate to a principal single-family dwelling. The property owner of record shall occupy either the accessory apartment or the principal single-family dwelling.

sections.title: Accessory Structure - A structure on the same lot with and of a nature which is
paragraphs: incidental and subordinate to the principal structure on the lot and which is typically associated with that principal structure. Accessory structures shall meet the same dimensional and yard requirements as the principal structure.

sections.title: Accessory Use
paragraphs: - A use of land or of a building or portion thereof incidental and subordinate to the principal use of the land or building and located on the same lot with the principal use.

sections.title: Adjacent
paragraphs: -- Contiguous parcels and parcels separated only by a public road, private road or right-of-way, railroad right-of-way, or riparian feature (river, stream, or brook).

sections.title: Agriculture or Farming
paragraphs: - Commercial production of crops (including, but not limited to horticultural, viticultural, floricultural, vegetable, berries, grain, hay and straw), dairy, maple, apiary, animal products, seed, Christmas trees and livestock, or any combination thereof, when not exempt from zoning review by 24 VSA 4413(d) or 10 VSA 6001 (22).

sections.title: Affordable Housing -- Housing that is occupied by inhabitants whose gross annual
paragraphs: household income does not exceed 80 percent of the county median income (or income of the standard metropolitan statistical area), and for which the total cost of the housing (as defined below) does not exceed 30 percent of the household's gross annual income. The long-term affordability of such units must be preserved through appropriate legal mechanisms. a. For owner occupied housing, total housing costs include mortgage principal, interest, taxes, insurance, and association fees. b. For renter occupied housing, total housing costs include rent, utilities, and association fees.

sections.title: Alteration - As applied to a building or structure, any change to the exterior or
paragraphs: structural elements of a building or structure. For the purposes of this definition, minor changes to elements such as painting, minor repairs, awnings, shutters or similar components shall not be considered an alteration. In the Village Design Review Overlay District, definitions set forth in Article XV shall apply. Page XXI- 1 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Art Gallery - A structure or portion thereof used for the display and/or sale of works of
paragraphs: art such as photographs, paintings, sculptures, woodworking, pottery, weavings, or jewelry.

sections.title: Artists' Studios - Spaces used by artists such as photographers, painters, sculptors,
paragraphs: woodworkers, potters, weavers, or jewelers, for the creation of their products or the teaching of their skills. Artists' studios may also contain a small area devoted to the display and sale of the products produced.

sections.title: Assisted Living Facility - An Elder Care Facility or facility providing Elderly
paragraphs: Supportive Service Housing.

sections.title: Automobile/Machinery Repair - The servicing, maintenance, or repair of
paragraphs: automobiles or small machinery, not including automobile body repair and painting.

sections.title: Banks or Other Financial Institutions - A business performing such services as
paragraphs: maintaining checking and savings accounts, making and administering loans, renting safe deposit boxes, cashing checks, and other similar services. Banks may include both drive- through and walk-in services, as well as automatic teller machines (ATMs).

sections.title: Bed and Breakfast - An owner occupied residential structure which contains sleeping
paragraphs: rooms for rent for transient occupancy. (See Articles describing individual zoning districts for specific regulations.)

sections.title: Buffer - An area of land generally kept in a natural state, used to visually separate
paragraphs: one use from another, to shield or block noise, lights, or other nuisances, or to protect a natural resource.

sections.title: Building or Structure - These terms are used interchangeably and mean any
paragraphs: construction, erection, assemblage or other combination of materials upon the land for occupancy or use, including without limitation, buildings, mobile homes, walls, fences, signs, antennas, swimming pools, tennis courts, driveways and utility sheds.

sections.title: Building Envelope - A defined three-dimensional (length, width, and height) space,
paragraphs: precisely located on a parcel of land and depicted on a relevant plan or plans, within which all structures on that parcel must be located.

sections.title: Building Material Sales - An establishment where one or more of a wide range of
paragraphs: building materials is provided and displayed for sale to both builders and the general public. Building materials may include such goods as lumber, nails and fasteners, tools, plumbing supplies, electrical supplies, doors, windows, floor coverings, paints, concrete block, stone, and the like.

sections.title: Business or Professional Office - A room or suite of rooms used for the conduct of
paragraphs: business, including administrative, executive, and support personnel, and/or space for Page XXI- 2 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016 working and meetings of professional people, their support staff, and their clients. Such office uses have limited contact with the general public and involve only limited on-site sales of goods directly to consumers.

sections.title: Campground - Land on which are located designated sites for recreational vehicles,
paragraphs: tents or other movable accommodations suitable for seasonal or temporary living purposes.

sections.title: Cutoff - A lighting fixture light distribution, specified by the IESNA, where the
paragraphs: intensity in candela per 1000 LAMP lumens does not numerically exceed 25 (2.5%) at a vertical angle of 90 degrees above nadir, and 100 (10 %) at a vertical angle of 80 degrees above nadir. Nadir is the point vertically below the lighting fixture.

sections.title: Cemeteries - A property used for the interment of the dead
Certificate of Occupancy - A document issued by the Zoning Administrative Officer
paragraphs: in accordance with 24 V.S.A., Section 4449 and the provisions of Article XX of these regulations, certifying that a structure or portion thereof has been developed in accord with all applicable local regulations, approvals, and permits, and authorizing the same to be used.

sections.title: Churches and Other Places of Worship - One or more structures or a portion of a
paragraphs: structure, used for the conduct of organized religious services, and associated accessory uses.

sections.title: Commercial Riding Stable - A stable for the for-profit boarding of equines and/or
paragraphs: associated accessory uses, including riding lessons, trail rides, or horse training.

sections.title: Community Farmers Market. - An occasional or periodic market, with goods offered
paragraphs: for sale to the general public by individual sellers from open-air or semi-enclosed facilities or temporary structures. The market is composed of five or more vendors with outside stalls, stands or spaces used for the purpose of display and sale, exchange, or barter of merchandise, which is limited to home produced or locally grown farm produce, and the incidental sale of artisan produced handiwork, artwork and food. Second-hand goods are not offered for sale.

sections.title: Construction Services Facilities - A facility serving as the headquarters or central
paragraphs: facility for a construction firm, which may include the parking of vehicles and/or the storage of equipment or materials.

sections.title: Continuing Care Retirement Community (CCRC) - A residential community
paragraphs: providing housing for the elderly (one resident in each unit being 60 or older) consisting of not more than 250 independent living units (in the form of either multi-family or single- family dwellings), associated common facilities primarily for the use of the CCRC residents, and a health center which may include facilities of the type offered in a community care home or nursing home for a maximum of 120 residents. Page XXI- 3 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Coverage, Building - The percentage of a lot's area which is occupied or covered by
paragraphs: buildings and other structures extending more than 12 inches above the existing grade at any point.

sections.title: Coverage, Lot - The percentage of a lot's area which is covered by buildings,
paragraphs: structures, parking areas, loading areas, paved or graveled driveways or other impervious surfaces.

sections.title: Day Care Center - A day care facility which provides care and protection to more
paragraphs: than 12 children

sections.title: Day Care Home (Licensed) - A day care facility that complies with licensing
paragraphs: standards. It may utilize two or more staff members and provide care and protection for not more than 12 children.

sections.title: Day Care Home (Registered Family) - A home which is described on the Family Day
paragraphs: Care Home Registration. The person issued the Family Day Care Home Registration is the primary provider of child care services. The Home allows for up to 6 pre-school children to attend for the day and up to 4 school age children to attend for 4 hours or less a day.

sections.title: Developable Land - Land that is suitable for development and which is not
paragraphs: characterized by any of the following: a. Slopes of 15 percent or more. b. Wetlands classified as class 2 or higher in the Vermont Significant Wetlands Inventory. c. Flood Plain identified in the most recent National Flood Insurance Program Maps. Undevelopable land shall not be considered when computing the maximum allowable dwelling units for any development.

sections.title: Development - See Land Development
Direct Light -- Light emitted directly from the lamp, from the reflector or reflector
paragraphs: diffuser, or through the refractor or diffuser lens of a lighting fixture.

sections.title: Dock -- A structure over or on water that may be used for the moorage of watercraft
paragraphs: Wood or metal structures mounted on piles or floats, piers, overhanging boat-house decks whose upper surfaces are within three feet of the water's surface and are accessible from the lake, and similar structures shall be considered docks for the purposes of these regulations.

sections.title: Drive-Through Pharmacy - A retail sales establishment which provides medicine and
paragraphs: other items, such as toiletries, various sundries and packaged foods for sale, and offers drop-off and pick-up service exclusively for prescriptions and associated medical items to persons within a motor vehicle. Page XXI- 4 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Dwelling Unit - A structure or self contained portion thereof, containing complete
paragraphs: housekeeping facilities for one family or household, and having no enclosed space in common with any other dwelling unit.

sections.title: Dwelling, Single-Family - A detached structure that contains a single dwelling unit
Dwelling, Two-Family - A structure containing two dwelling units, designed for
paragraphs: occupancy by not more than two families.

sections.title: Dwelling, Multi-Family - A residential building designed for and occupied by three
paragraphs: or more families, with the number of families in residence not exceeding the number of dwelling units provided.

sections.title: Dwelling, Seasonal - A dwelling unit that is used or approved for use for no more
paragraphs: than six months of any twelve month period.

sections.title: Dwelling, Year Round - A dwelling unit that is used or approved for use on a year
paragraphs: round basis.

sections.title: Elder Care Facility - An establishment that provides housing and care for persons of
paragraphs: 55 years of age or older who cannot or choose to not live independently. Housing units, which must be less than 800 square feet in size, are not complete dwelling units in that they lack facilities adequate to prepare meals on a regular basis, and communal dining and living spaces are provided. Care can range from periodic assistance with medication to skilled nursing care.

sections.title: Elder Housing - Housing that is:
paragraphs: (1) intended for, and solely occupied by, persons 62 years of age or older; or (2) intended and operated for occupancy by at least one person 55 years of age or older per unit, provided all of the following conditions are met: (A) The housing complex has significant facilities and services specifically designed to meet the physical or social needs of older persons, or if it is not practicable to provide those facilities and services, that the housing complex is necessary to provide important housing opportunities for older persons; (B) By no later than the date on which the occupancy level first reaches 25 percent of units, at least 80 percent of occupied units must be occupied by at least one person 55 years of age or older per unit; and (C) There are written and enforced policies and procedures which demonstrate an intent by the owner or manager to provide housing for persons 55 years of age or older.

sections.title: Elderly Supportive Service Housing - Housing that is occupied by inhabitants over
paragraphs: the age of 55 in individual housing units containing less than 1,000 square feet within one Page XXI- 5 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016 structure which also includes common areas for living, dining and activities. The individual housing units may contain kitchen, bathroom, living area and bedroom(s). Optional independent living services such as meals, social activities and health and wellness services may be offered on-site.

sections.title: Erosion - Erosion means when land is diminished or worn due to wind or water
paragraphs: Often the eroded debris (silt or sediment) becomes a pollutant via stormwater runoff. Erosion occurs naturally but can be intensified by land clearing activities such as farming, development, road building, and timber harvesting.

sections.title: Erosion and sediment control plan - A plan that indicates the specific measures and
paragraphs: their sequencing for use to control sediment and erosion on a development site during and after construction. and approved by an authorized enforcement agency

sections.title: Family - An individual, or two or more persons related by blood, marriage, civil
paragraphs: union, legal adoption, or those placed in a home for adoption, and foster children, or a group of not more than five persons who need not be related by civil union, blood, or marriage, living together as a single housekeeping unit.

sections.title: Farm Labor Dwelling - A dwelling unit, located on an active farm operation, used as
paragraphs: housing for a farm employee working on the farm, and members of the employee's immediate family.

sections.title: Fire/Rescue Station - A building housing municipally operated or supported fire
paragraphs: protection or rescue operations, including but not limited to storage of vehicles and equipment, training space and facilities, eating and sitting areas, locker rooms, sleeping rooms, radio/communications systems, and the like.

sections.title: Fire Protected Structure - A building that incorporates the following features:
paragraphs: Compliant with the requirements of NFPA 13 including an attic sprinkler system, a Stand Pipe system, a Stortz connection and a fully enunciated fire alarm system with dial-out capabilities. The building construction shall be designed such that: 1-hr rated envelopes are created around each residential unit; no roof top mechanicals are located above 35'; no fireplaces shall be installed in residential units (gas fireplaces shall be allowed in common areas); electric ranges shall be used in residential units; and an elevator of such size suitable for handling a patient on a stretcher in the supine (flat) position shall be installed. Outside the building, 20' wide stabilized surfaces shall be provided for fire truck access to locations as approved by the Fire Chief.

sections.title: Foot Candle -- Unit of illuminance; One lumen per square foot
Full Cutoff -- A lighting fixture light distribution, specified by the Illuminating
paragraphs: Engineering Society of North America, where zero candela intensity occurs at an angle of 90 degrees above nadir, and at all greater angles from nadir. Additionally, the candela per 1000 lamp lumens does not numerically exceed 100 (10 percent) at a vertical angle of 80 Page XXI- 6 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016 degrees above nadir. Nadir is the point vertically below the light fixture. A full cutoff lighting fixture is fully shielded.

sections.title: Fully Shielded -- Constructed in such a manner that no light emitted by the fixture,
paragraphs: either directly from the lamp or a diffusing element, or indirectly by reflection or refraction from any part of the lighting fixture, is projected above a horizontal plane passing through the lowest direct-light-emitting part of the fixture.

sections.title: Gasoline Station - A building or land containing at least one fuel pump, used for the
paragraphs: commercial sale of vehicular fuel (gasoline, diesel, etc.) to private vehicle owners, and which may include facilities for installation of lubricants, tires, batteries, etc., and routine maintenance of vehicles.

sections.title: Gasoline Station Canopy - An attached or detached structure providing cover and
paragraphs: under which vehicles park while fueling.

sections.title: Garden Center/Nursery - A building and lands used for the storage, display and sales
paragraphs: of garden supplies such as soils, fertilizers, garden tools, landscaping materials, etc., and/or the growing and sale of plant materials.

sections.title: Glare -- The sensation of visual discomfort or loss in visual performance and
paragraphs: visibility produced by luminance within the visual field that is sufficiently greater the luminance to which the eyes are adapted.

sections.title: Grain - A term describing a visual quality of development, referring to the size and
paragraphs: frequency of building masses and open areas, and to the degree of detail in the architectural treatment of the facades. A fine grain is typical of more urban settings and reflects smaller visual building units, small spaces between them, and a high degree of detail in the façade treatment. A large grain is typical of exurban and suburban settings with large buildings, large spaces between buildings, and relatively little architectural detail on the facades. A fine grained setting exhibits more human or pedestrian scale.

sections.title: Group/Residential Care Home - A place, however named, excluding a licensed foster
paragraphs: home, which provides, for profit or otherwise, room, board and personal care to not more than 8 residents.

sections.title: Height - The vertical distance of a structure as measured from the average (of the
paragraphs: lowest and highest elevation points) of the finished grade where it meets any wall of the proposed building, to the midpoint of the eave and ridge of the structure. Chimneys (except chimneys on residential structures) and similar structures shall be subject to the height limitations contained in these regulations.

sections.title: Home Occupation - An occupation, carried on within a minor portion of a dwelling
paragraphs: by a resident of the dwelling unit, that is customary in residential areas and that does not Page XXI- 7 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016 have an undue adverse effect on the character of the residential area in which the dwelling is located.

sections.title: Hotel or Motel - A facility, other than a bed and breakfast or inn or campground or
paragraphs: rooming house, that offers transient lodging accommodations on a daily or weekly rate, to the general public, and which may also provide additional services such as restaurants, meeting rooms, or recreation facilities. As motel, at least half of all lodging rooms shall have direct access to the outside without passing through a lobby or common corridor. A Hotel/Motel may include a single accessory residential unit for use by a facility manager.

sections.title: Household - See family
Housing for the Elderly - See Elder Housing
Human Scale - A building and its details, as they relate to human scale proportions;
paragraphs: also, a building's mass and bulk and the building's details proportionately compared with other buildings in the surrounding area or neighborhood.

sections.title: Illuminance -- The luminous flux incident per unit area, expressed in foot candles
paragraphs: Horizontal or vertical illuminance is that measured with a photometer cell mounted horizontally or vertically.

sections.title: Impervious Surface - Any surface through which water does not readily pass
paragraphs: Impervious surfaces shall include (but are not limited to) concrete or asphalt paving, compressed gravel, brick or stone pavers, cobble stones, or other hard surfaces.

sections.title: Incidental - Being of nature that is both minor in relationship to and in consequence
paragraphs: of some other object, action, or state; and where, in the absence of the other object, action, or state, that thing which is incidental would not occur independently.

sections.title: Indirect Light -- Direct light that has been reflected off the surface of any
paragraphs: permanently constructed object other than the source lighting fixture.

sections.title: Indoor Movie Theater - A building or portion thereof used for showing motion
paragraphs: pictures to the general public.

sections.title: Indoor Storage in Agricultural Structures - The use of an agricultural structure
paragraphs: existing on March 17, 2009, for leased storage of property, vehicles, equipment, and similar items.

sections.title: Inn - A facility other than a Bed and Breakfast, hotel, or motel, or rooming house
paragraphs: and having no more than 8 guest rooms, that provides rental lodging accommodations to the general public on a daily or weekly basis, and which may provide meals to lodging guests. Page XXI- 8 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Integrated Agriculture - Hybrid land use and development incidental and directly
paragraphs: related to the principal farming activity being conducted on-site excluding the slaughter of livestock or poultry and consisting of the following "Primary Integrated Agricultural Activities": * The on-site preparation and processing of crops or produce not principally produced on the farm; * The storage and sale of crops or produce not principally produced on the farm or the resulting products from such crops or produce; * The sampling and tasting of crops and produce not principally produced on the farm or the resulting products from such crops or produce; and/or * Tours of growing areas and storage and processing facilities.

sections.title: Kennels - A building, or portion thereof, and grounds used for the commercial
paragraphs: boarding of dogs, cats, or other small domestic animals. Kennels board such animals over night. The use may include accessory activities such as grooming and training.

sections.title: Lakeshore Erosion Control Structure- Structure, device, or material assembled or
paragraphs: installed to prevent or limit erosion along Lake Champlain shoreline.

sections.title: Lakeside Deck- A roofless outdoor space built as an above-ground platform, used for
paragraphs: sitting or passive recreational purposes associated with proximity to a lake or pond, and which is separated from any residential primary structure by a distance of at least ten feet.

sections.title: Lakeside Wall- Any wall of a primary structure located within 100 feet of the 102
paragraphs: foot elevation contour along Lake Champlain, where said wall is parallel with or generally parallel with the Lake and reflects the overall orientation of the structure to the Lake. See Figures D and E.

sections.title: Lamp - The light source component of a lighting fixture that produces the actual
paragraphs: light.

sections.title: Land Development - Consistent with 24 V.S.A., 4303(10), land development shall
paragraphs: mean the division of a parcel into two or more parcels, the construction, reconstruction, conversion, structural alteration, relocation, or enlargement of any building or other structure, or of any mining, excavation, or landfill, and any change in the use of any building or other structure, or land, or extension of use of land. Land development shall include the construction or establishment of any exterior lighting installation totaling more than 100 watts, except as may be authorized by any specific lighting regulations adopted by the Town.

sections.title: Landscaping - The improvement of a lot, parcel or tract of land with grass and shrubs
paragraphs: and/or trees. Landscaping may include flower beds, pedestrian walks, retaining walls under 24 inches in height, statues and other similar ornamental objects. Page XXI- 9 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Libraries - A building, or portion thereof, used for the storage, display, and lending
paragraphs: of books and other audio/visual media. A library may include, among other spaces, reading space, meeting space, study rooms, shelving areas, work areas, and administrative areas.

sections.title: Light Manufacturing - A building, or portion thereof, used for the fabrication and
paragraphs: assembly of products, either for direct consumption or for use in other assembly processes. Light manufacturing uses may include metal fabrication, welding, dry cleaning and other processes, precision machine fabrication, and similar fabrication activities, and manufacturing of food products, excluding slaughterhouses.

sections.title: Lighting Fixture - A complete outdoor lighting unit including a lamp or lamps,
paragraphs: together with the parts designed to distribute the light, to position and protect the lamps, and to connect the lamps to the power supply, but not including a pole on which the lighting fixture may be mounted.

sections.title: Light Trespass -- Direct or indirect light produced by an artificial light source and
paragraphs: which shines outside the boundaries of the lot containing the lighting fixture.

sections.title: Lot - A parcel of land (other than a pre-existing small lot) of at least sufficient size to
paragraphs: meet the minimum zoning requirements for use, coverage and area, and to provide such yards and other open spaces as required by these regulations.

sections.title: Lot, Corner - A lot located at the intersection of two streets or roads. A corner lot
paragraphs: shall be deemed to have front yards facing both streets or roads.

sections.title: Lot, Through - A lot that extends the full distance between two parallel or roughly
paragraphs: parallel streets or roads and has frontage on both. The developer/owner of a through lot may choose which frontage will be treated as the front yard.

sections.title: Lot Frontage - The length of the boundary of a lot which fronts a public street,
paragraphs: waterway, or (when approved by the Development Review Board) a private road or right- of-way, from which primary access to the principal structure on the lot is obtained. When access to a lot is provided by a road or right of way oriented perpendicular to rather than parallel with the lot boundary, the lot shall be considered to have no frontage and thus the lot shall be exempt from lot frontage dimensional requirements.

sections.title: Lot Width - The minimum distance between any points on the side boundaries of a
paragraphs: lot as measured parallel to the lot frontage line. For irregularly shaped lots in the Rural District, lot width shall be as defined in Article III.

sections.title: Lumber Yard - A type of building material sales establishments specializing in
paragraphs: dimensional lumber and other construction lumber, but may include a limited number of associated items such as wood fasteners, ladders, and light hardware. Page XXI- 10 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Marinas - The use of land and/or buildings for the manufacture or construction, sale,
paragraphs: or repair of boats, along with associated derricks, docks, wharfs, marine railways, boat storage areas and marina facilities for the commercial servicing, maintenance, storage, docking of vessels or the furnishing of general marine services. A marina may include sales of food or other items to marina patrons, provided that such sales activities are clearly incidental to the operation of the other marine base activities.

sections.title: Medical or dental offices - A room or suite of rooms used for the provision of
paragraphs: medical, dental or other health care services, including waiting rooms, records rooms, reception areas, examination rooms, laboratories, and equipment customarily associated with the provision of health care.

sections.title: Mobile Home - A single story structure that is transportable in one or more sections
paragraphs: and designed for single family residential use with or without a permanent foundation when attached to the required utilities. A mobile home may be built on a permanent chassis. A mobile home does not include a "recreational vehicle."

sections.title: Mobile Home Park - Any parcel of land under a single or common ownership or
paragraphs: control, which contains, or is designed, laid out or adapted to accommodate, two or more mobile homes, but not including premises for the display or storage of mobile homes.

sections.title: Multiple-Family Dwelling- See Dwelling, Multi-Family
Multiple Uses - Any combination of permitted or conditional uses allowed under the
paragraphs: designated zoning district.

sections.title: Municipal Offices - A building, or portion thereof, used for administrative functions
paragraphs: of the Town government or School District.

sections.title: Museums - One or more buildings and associated grounds used for the display,
paragraphs: exhibition, storage, interpretation, and preservation of objects illustrating human endeavor and/or natural history, and associated activities such as administration, education, and visitor amenities (including gift and food sales to visitors).

sections.title: National Geodetic Vertical Datum (NGVD) - The vertical control datum established
paragraphs: for vertical control surveying in the United States of America.

sections.title: No-Cut Zone - A delineated portion of a lot or parcel of land, designated in an
paragraphs: approved permit, subdivision or site plan, within which no living vegetation may be cut, pruned, removed or destroyed.

sections.title: Nonconformities - In accordance with 24 V.S.A., Section 4303, Nonconformities
paragraphs: shall mean nonconforming lots, structures, or uses. Page XXI- 11 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Nonconforming Lot - A lot that does not conform to the present bylaws covering
paragraphs: dimensional requirements but which was in conformance with all applicable laws, ordinances, and regulations prior to the enactment of the present bylaws, including a lot improperly authorized as a result of error by the administrative officer.

sections.title: Nonconforming Structure - A structure or part of a structure that does not conform to
paragraphs: the present bylaws but which was in conformance with all applicable laws, ordinances, and regulations prior to the enactment of the present bylaws, including a structure improperly authorized as a result of error by the administrative officer.

sections.title: Nonconforming Use - A use of land that does not conform to the present bylaws but
paragraphs: did conform to all applicable laws, ordinances, and regulations prior to the enactment of the present bylaws, including a use improperly authorized as a result of error by the administrative officer

sections.title: Nursing Home - A place, other than a hospital, which maintains and operates
paragraphs: facilities and provides skilled nursing care, for profit or otherwise, and is licensed to provide such care by the State of Vermont. The forgoing shall not be construed to prevent the care of a person(s) related to the occupant of a dwelling.

sections.title: Open space - Land which, in connection with a development proposal, is set aside
paragraphs: from development by conveyance to the Town or some qualified holder, or by some legal mechanism such as covenants or easements, and designated to remain in its natural state (woodland, meadow land, wetland, etc.), agricultural use, or for active or passive outdoor recreation uses.

sections.title: Outdoor Pet Exercise Area - A portion of a parcel approved for use as a Pet Care
paragraphs: Facility or Kennel, and which is used on a daily or weekly basis by dogs, cats, or other small domestic animals for recreation, socialization, evacuation, or excretion.

sections.title: Parcel - An area of land in one ownership, completely surrounded by boundary lines
paragraphs: An area of land in one ownership that is traversed by a public road shall be considered as two parcels.

sections.title: Parking Space - An area of land , not less than 9 feet wide and 18 feet in length,
paragraphs: suitable and available for the temporary parking of one motor vehicle.

sections.title: Personal Service Shop - A building, or portion thereof, used for the provision of
paragraphs: services of a personal nature to individuals, including but not limited to barber shops, beauty shops, clothing repair shops, shoe repair shops, dry cleaning drop-offs (where actual cleaning is done elsewhere), and the like.

sections.title: Pet Care Facilities - A building, or portion thereof, used for the commercial
paragraphs: boarding, recreation, and socialization of dogs, cats, or other small domestic animals. Pet Page XXI- 12 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016 Care Facilities may board such animals overnight but must do so indoors. Animals may be walked out of doors when under the direct supervision of a staff member or the animal's owner.

sections.title: Planned Unit Development - One or more lots to be developed as a single entity
paragraphs: according to a plan approved in accordance with Article XIX of these Regulations. If authorized in Article XIX, a Planned Unit Development Plan may contain a mix of uses, and may deviate from bylaw requirements otherwise applicable regarding lot size, bulk, type of dwelling or building, use density, intensity, lot coverage, parking, required open space, or other standards.

sections.title: Post Office Sorting Facility, U.S. - A building or portion thereof used primarily for
paragraphs: the sorting of large volumes of mail by the U. S. Postal Service, but which may include associated space for direct service of customers such as sales of stamps and/or receipt of objects for mailing.

sections.title: Post Office Store - A building or portion thereof used primarily for the direct sale of
paragraphs: postal services to customers, including receipt of objects to be mailed, sale of stamps, sale of packaging, provision of rental post office boxes. The facility may include some space devoted to sorting mail dropped off at the store or to be delivered to post office boxes at the store, or to be delivered to nearby neighborhoods.

sections.title: Police Station - A building or portion thereof housing municipally operated police
paragraphs: operations, including but not limited to storage of vehicles and equipment, training space and facilities, eating and sitting areas, locker/shower rooms, interrogation rooms, detention facilities, associated work spaces, radio/communications systems, and other activities associated with police services.

sections.title: Private Guest House - A detached structure located on the same lot as a single family
paragraphs: dwelling, used intermittently to provide temporary lodging, on a not-for-hire basis, to invitees of the residents or owners of the single family dwelling.

sections.title: Public and General Aviation Use Airport - A facility intended and used as a place
paragraphs: where one or more fixed wing or rotary wing aircraft are regularly stored, maintained or repaired while not in flight, including the areas that the aircraft may use to take off and land. Subject to availability, airport uses may be available to the public.

sections.title: Public and General Aviation Airport Uses - A use or uses customarily conducted at
paragraphs: Public and General Aviation Use Airports, including operations related to public, private and general aviation, including aircraft sales, fueling, repair, storage, shipping, rental, flight instruction, and other uses designed to serve aviation passengers and pilots.

sections.title: Public Utility Facilities - A building or portion thereof housing administrative
paragraphs: offices or equipment associated with the provision of utilities such as energy or communications. Page XXI- 13 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Re-build - The re-establishment of a structure following whole or partial demolition
paragraphs: by fire or other natural disaster. Except as may be authorized under "non-conformities" (Section 1920 of these Regulations), a re-build will be subject to all applicable dimensional requirements set forth in these Regulations.

sections.title: Reconstruction -- The planned demolition of an existing structure or part thereof and
paragraphs: construction of one or more new structures on the site. Unless expressly authorized elsewhere, reconstruction shall be subject to all requirements of these regulations.

sections.title: Recreation, Indoor - A building or portion thereof containing recreation facilities
paragraphs: including but not limited to swimming pools, skating rinks, gymnasia, bowling alleys, fitness centers, training rooms, playing fields, tennis courts, handball/racquet ball/squash courts, volley ball courts, and associated locker rooms, dressing areas, shower/steam bath/sauna spaces and administrative spaces.

sections.title: Recreation, Outdoor - One or more parcels used for outdoor recreation activities
paragraphs: Outdoor recreation activities may range from passive (Those requiring no substantial alteration or maintenance of the land such as primitive hiking trails) to active (those requiring substantial alteration or maintenance of the land such as developed parks, organized athletic facilities, VAST trails, ski runs, etc.). * Outdoor recreation facilities with no structures may include minimal structures such as occasional benches and bridges taking trails over streams. * Outdoor recreation facilities with minor structures may include such associated structures as backstops, dugouts, fences, storage buildings, portable ice rinks, warming huts and the like. * Outdoor recreation facilities with major structures may include such structures as clubhouses/lodges, or locker/dressing rooms. See Articles describing individual zoning districts for detailed restrictions.

sections.title: Recreational Vehicle - A vehicle without permanent foundation, which can be towed,
paragraphs: hauled or driven, which is designed to be used as temporary living accommodations for camping and travel, including but not limited to travel trailers, truck campers, camping trailers and self propelled motor homes.

sections.title: Redevelopment -- The adaptation of an existing structure for contemporary uses,
paragraphs: including the gutting and reorganization of internal spaces and the replacement of exterior elements.

sections.title: Research and Testing laboratories - A building or portion thereof used for
paragraphs: conducting and reporting scientific tests, including offices, laboratories, storage, computer facilities, libraries, and associated activities. Page XXI- 14 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Restaurant - An establishment where food and drink are prepared to order, served and
paragraphs: consumed primarily within the principal building or in designated outdoor eating areas, and excluding fast food restaurants. A restaurant may also serve customers on a "phone in/pick up" basis.

sections.title: Restaurant, fast food - An establishment whose principal business is the sale of food
paragraphs: or beverages, for consumption either on or off the premises, and whose operation demonstrates at least three of the following four characteristics: (1) service of food or beverage predominantly in paper, plastic or other disposable containers, (2) availability of food or beverages for immediate consumption upon short waiting time, (3) insufficient seating facilities within the building for the volume of food sold, or (4) a drive through service window.

sections.title: Retail Sales - The sale of goods or merchandise to the general public for personal or
paragraphs: household consumption (including services incidental to such sales).

sections.title: Roadside Farm Stand - A small building or open air stand used for the seasonal sale
paragraphs: of locally grown farm produce.

sections.title: Rooming House - An owner occupied structure containing rooms for lease to short
paragraphs: or long term guests, and in which meals may be provided to the guests.

sections.title: School - An establishment or facility which provides education or training to students
paragraphs: in an organized way. A school may be public or private. A school may include support facilities such as gymnasia, play fields, laboratories, kitchens, cafeteria, libraries, auditoria, offices, etc.

sections.title: Screening - A method of visually shielding or obscuring one abutting or nearby
paragraphs: structure or parcel from another. Screening may be achieved by the use of one or a combination of fencing, walls, berms/mounds, or densely planted vegetation.

sections.title: Seasonal Dwelling - See Dwelling, Seasonal
Seawall - A type of lakeshore erosion control structure located at waters edge built
paragraphs: to protect the shoreline from erosion due to wave action or prevent flooding.

sections.title: Sediment - Soil, sand, and minerals washed from land into water, usually after rain
paragraphs: Sediment can destroy fish-nesting areas, clog animal habitats, and cloud water so that sunlight does not reach aquatic plants.

sections.title: Sediment control - Measures that prevent eroded sediment from leaving a site
Setback - The distance from any property line or street right-of-way line to the
paragraphs: nearest point of a building on the lot bounded by that property line or street line, including Page XXI- 15 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016 decks but excluding: (A) eaves, sills, pilasters, gutters, leaders, cornices, chimneys, and roof overhangs provided such features do not extend more than three (3) feet from the remainder of the structure; (B) uncovered steps to first floor entries provided such features do not extend more than five (5) feet from the remainder of the structure; (C) retrofit modifications to a structure made for energy efficiency purposes, provided that such features do not extend more than eight (8) inches from the remainder of the structure ; and (D) handicapped access ramps.

sections.title: Signs - Any advertisement, announcement, direction or communication produced in
paragraphs: whole or in part by the construction, erection, affixing, or placing of a structure on any land or on any other structure, or produced by painting on or posting or placing any printed, lettered, pictured, figured, or colored material on any building, structure or surface, or produced by projecting an image upon the exterior of any building or structure.

sections.title: Sign, Facade - A sign attached to, painted on, or erected against the wall of a building
paragraphs: or structure with the exposed face of the sign in a plane parallel to the face of said wall, which is placed in view of the general public from outside the building or structure.

sections.title: Sign, Projection - A sign attached to a building or other structure and extending in
paragraphs: whole or in part more than 9 inches beyond the building wall.

sections.title: Staff Quarters - An accessory single family dwelling, located on the same parcel as a
paragraphs: primary single family dwelling, used to provide permanent housing for full time staff employed on the premises and their families.

sections.title: Stormwater- Any surface flow, runoff, and drainage consisting entirely of water from
paragraphs: any form of natural precipitation, and resulting from such precipitation.

sections.title: Stormwater Management - The use of structural or non-structural practices that are
paragraphs: designed to reduce stormwater runoff pollutant loads, discharge volumes, and/or peak flow discharge rates.

sections.title: Stormwater Treatment Practices - Measures, either structural or non-structural, that
paragraphs: are determined to be the most effective, practical means of preventing or reducing point source or nonpoint source pollution inputs to stormwater runoff and water bodies.

sections.title: Stormwater Impaired Waters- A water body currently identified by the Vermont
paragraphs: Department of Environmental Conservation following the requirements of the Clean Water Act Section 303(d)

sections.title: Structure - See Building
Subordinate - Being of markedly less or of secondary importance relative to another
paragraphs: object, action, or state. Page XXI- 16 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Town Garage - Land and/or buildings used by a municipality for the storage, care,
paragraphs: and maintenance of equipment, vehicles, and supplies associated with the use and maintenance of public buildings, roadways, or facilities.

sections.title: Transit Passenger Station - A facility designed to accommodate people boarding and
paragraphs: de-boarding public transit vehicles, including an enclosed waiting space, facilities for the sale of tickets or tokens, and parking. A street-side bus stop with a shelter shall not be construed as a transit passenger station.

sections.title: Truck Gardening - Small scale form of farming in which fruits and /or vegetables
paragraphs: are grown for market, distinguishable from other types of farming by the diversity of crops grown on a small area of land.

sections.title: Upholstery/Fabric Working - The use of a building or portion thereof for the creation
paragraphs: of such fabric based products as upholstery, awnings, tents, canopies, vehicle covers, and the like.

sections.title: Use - The specific purpose for which land or a building or a portion thereof is
paragraphs: designated, arranged, or intended, or for which it is or may be occupied or maintained.

sections.title: Vehicle sales and repair - A facility for the sale and repair of motorized vehicles or
paragraphs: equipment or mobile homes. Typical uses include new and used automobile and recreational vehicle sales and repair, and trailered boat sales and repair. Small engine vehicles and machinery which are typically displayed in enclosed structures and boat sales which are accessory to a marina are not included in this definition.

sections.title: Veterinary Clinic - A building or portion thereof used for the provision of veterinary
paragraphs: care to domestic animals. A veterinary clinic may include waiting areas, record storage areas, examination rooms, surgeries, spaces for animals in cages, and associated uses.

sections.title: Warehouse - A building or portion thereof used on a commercial basis for the short
paragraphs: or long term storage of goods.

sections.title: Waste Water Treatment Plant - One or more structures, operating under a state
paragraphs: permit or license, used to treat wastewater prior to discharging it into receiving waters.

sections.title: Watershed - That geographical area that drains to a specified point on a watercourse,
paragraphs: usually a confluence of streams or rivers

sections.title: Wholesale Sales - The use of a building or portion thereof for the sale of goods to
paragraphs: other entities that then use them as part of a fabrication process or resell them to the direct consumers. Page XXI- 17 SHELBURNE ZONING BYLAW ARTICLE XXI (DEFINITIONS) Effective May 18, 2016

sections.title: Wildlife Management/Refuge Areas - Areas which have been protected against
paragraphs: future development and which are being managed and used for wildlife habitat and/or as refuge areas for wildlife.

sections.title: Windmills - Devices, including their towers, which convert wind energy to electrical
paragraphs: or mechanical energy.

sections.title: Yacht Club - Land and buildings used to provide boating related services to club
paragraphs: members. A yacht club may include docks, mooring areas, launch services, seasonal small boat storage, parking areas, clubhouses, small play fields, etc., but may not include winter storage of boats or commercial repair activities.

sections.title: Yard - An open space on a lot, unoccupied and unobstructed from the ground upward
paragraphs: by any building or structure, except as otherwise provided in these regulations.

sections.title: Yard, front - a yard on the same lot with a principal building, extending the full width
paragraphs: of the lot and situated between the right-of-way line of the public road, private road, or Right-of-way, from which primary access to the principal structure on the lot is obtained and the front line of the building extended to the sidelines of the lot.

sections.title: Yard, rear - A yard on the same lot with a principal building between the rear line of
paragraphs: the building and the rear line of the lot extending the full length of the lot.

sections.title: Yard, side - A yard situated between the principal building and a sideline and
paragraphs: extending from the front yard to the rear yard. The distance between the principal building and the sideline shall be measured from the building to the nearest point on the sideline along a line parallel to the front lot line.

sections.title: Zoning/Building Permit - In accordance with 24 V.S.A., Section 4449, a permit
paragraphs: issued by the Zoning Administrative Officer in accordance with the provisions of Article XX of these regulations, which authorizes specified land development and which may contain conditions which must be met in order for the land development to comply with the provisions of these regulations and any applicable approvals.
